title: Localize the bottleneck with reciprocal post-lift handoffs
hypothesis: Assembly fails because of post-lift control rather than irreversible grasp errors, so an expert suffix can complete learner-produced grasps.

prediction.against: baseline: uninterrupted execution of the two frozen D-020 assembly policies
prediction.rationale: A 30-point gain would identify a recoverable post-lift bottleneck; success must come without releasing and regrasping the nut.

code_changes: lares/repair/interventions.py (HandoffActor: one state-triggered handoff between a policy and the scripted expert)

falsified_by: With a reliable full expert, the upper paired confidence bound for learner-prefix/expert-suffix improvement is below 0.30. An interval including zero is inconclusive; the resolving measurement is the same paired handoff contrast on another fresh 30-case development manifest.

approval.note: approved by advisor gpt-6.1-sol (consult call_00043, 'revise' with changes applied) under the user's 2026-10-22 session delegation

controls.note: control is uninterrupted execution of the same frozen D-020 policy on the same cases; the metric is already learner-then-expert minus uninterrupted

result.notes: Frozen D-020 winners rebuilt deterministically (hashes recorded); development cases 10-39 of a fresh assembly-v2 pool (seed 3400). Full expert 1.00, so localization is valid. Learner-then-expert (handoff when the nut is >= 3 cm above its start and the gripper within 4 cm for 3 steps) minus uninterrupted: +0.333 [+0.244, +0.423], averaged over the two fixed structures. The handoff fired in every episode for both structures. Per structure: assembly_repeat 0.00 -> 0.67 (the expert completes most learner grasps: a post-lift placement bottleneck); assembly_first 0.00 -> 0.00 (the expert cannot recover its grasps: a grasp-configuration failure). Expert-then-learner never handed off (the expert's own trajectory never met the trigger, it ran to completion and scored 1.00), so that reciprocal arm is uninformative. 210 episodes, 0 LLM calls.

verdicts.reasoning: With a reliable expert (1.00), handing control to the expert after the learner's lift raises success by +0.333 [+0.244, +0.423] over uninterrupted execution, meeting the predicted +0.30 with a positive lower bound. The average hides a split: one structure's grasps are recoverable (0.00 -> 0.67: a post-lift placement bottleneck), the other's are not (0.00 -> 0.00: the grasp configuration itself fails). The reciprocal arm is uninformative because the expert never met the trigger. Conclusion is conditional on these two structures.
verdicts.next_experiment: Target the post-lift placement phase for structures like assembly_repeat (e.g. placement-phase repair or fitting on expert placement data), and check grasp configuration for structures like assembly_first; R-026 (expert-gradient fitting vs numerical search) is approved and next.

verdicts.reasoning: The quantitative prediction held: paired_success_difference was +0.333 against uninterrupted execution of the same frozen policies, exceeding the predicted +0.30 [logs/assembly_handoff_s3400/summary.json]. Its interval [+0.244, +0.423] excludes zero, supporting an improvement, but does not establish that the underlying gain exceeds +0.30 [logs/assembly_handoff_s3400/summary.json]. The gain was structure-specific: assembly_repeat improved by +0.667, while assembly_first tied its control at zero success and provides no improvement evidence [logs/assembly_handoff_s3400/summary.json]. Full-expert success was 1.00, but expert-then-learner never handed off, so that reciprocal arm cannot localize the failure [logs/assembly_handoff_s3400/summary.json]. The reported metrics do not verify success without release/regrasp or distinguish irreversible grasp errors from expert recovery limitations, so the broader mechanistic hypothesis remains unresolved [logs/assembly_handoff_s3400/summary.json].
